solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Greeks' opponents according to Welsh lady and son

parts.note: per is Latin-derived for 'according to', as in 'per the rules'
Sian (Siân) is a common Welsh woman's name
S is the standard abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman and her boy apparently have views on who stood against the ancient Greeks.
explanation.definitionFit: The armies of the Achaemenid empire fought the Greek city-states at Marathon, Thermopylae and Salamis.

clue.text: Sweetheart (honey) conceals where we live

indicators.note: conceals says the letters sit tucked away inside the words before it, running from one into the next

explanation.surface: A lover's endearment seems to be hiding something about our home.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the end of 'Sweetheart' and the start of 'honey'; the brackets are only surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Our home planet is the place where all of us live, a light cryptic paraphrase.

clue.text: At first Napoleon, alien, hates being redeployed here?

definitions.text: At first Napoleon, alien, hates being redeployed here?

indicators.note: redeployed means rearranged into new positions, so the letters gathered are shuffled
At first picks out only the opening letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: Napoleon, an outsider on a remote island he loathes, ends up posted there: a sketch of his final exile.
explanation.walkthrough: N (first of Napoleon) plus ALIEN and HATES are shuffled, signalled by 'being redeployed'; the whole clue also describes the place, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Atlantic island was where the British exiled the deposed French emperor until his death in 1821.

clue.text: Article (leading) I see describing chaos

parts.note: arch means chief or principal, as in arch-rival
C stands for see, as in a text abbreviation, since the letter sounds the same

explanation.surface: Someone notes that an article in the lead position is about disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: '(leading)' looks like a newspaper's lead article, but it is ARCH, as in archbishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawless, disorderly conditions are what this adjective portrays, so it describes chaos.

clue.text: New version of iconic clue (rusty) needed for New York based body

indicators.note: a new version is the same material reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter admits an out-of-practice clue needs rewriting for an American organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'New version of' uses the first 'New'; the second 'New' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The UN organ that keeps international peace meets at the United Nations headquarters in Manhattan.

clue.text: Note position — classy environment

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
lie means the way something is placed, as in the lie of the land
U means upper-class, the old label for posh usage

explanation.surface: A memo about where someone stands in a refined setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classy' gives U, from the 1950s U and non-U division of upper-class and other usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words denote the social surroundings or setting in which a person lives or works.

clue.text: Some rising belle or no mean US actress?

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wry question whether some up-and-coming beauty might be a notable American film star.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' means read upwards, so EORNOM, found inside the words, becomes the actress's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn was the famous Hollywood star of Some Like It Hot and Gentlemen Prefer Blondes.

clue.text: Regularly visited Liege for shelter

indicators.note: only the letters at regular intervals in the Belgian city's name are called on

explanation.surface: A traveller kept going to the Belgian city of Liège for refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: The first, third and fifth letters of Liege are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheltered side of something, away from the wind, gives protection, as in the lee of a hill.

clue.text: Nurses' act upset old Italians

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disarranged, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A news line: the conduct of hospital staff has offended some Italians of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient people of central Italy, around Tuscany, flourished before Rome absorbed them.

clue.text: Group from east in Nagasaki or Tokyo

indicators.note: from east says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A news item about a group from the east, based in one of two Japanese cities.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, reading from the east means right to left; 'in' points to letters inside 'Nagasaki or Tokyo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a group of three acting together, from the Russian three-horse team.

clue.text: Is able to book artist after hesitation in capital

indicators.note: after places the artist's letters behind those of the hesitation

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone can reserve a painter, after some dithering, in a major city.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the seat of government of Australia, hence its national capital.

clue.text: Talk about Derby maybe

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a derby is a bowler, one kind of headwear

explanation.surface: A prompt to discuss the Derby, the famous English horse race, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous English horse race, but here it is the American name for a bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to converse informally, as in having a natter with a friend.

clue.text: One drawing finding traction so troublesome?

indicators.note: troublesome suggests disorder, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone pulling a load finds it hard going because the grip is so poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests pulling, matching 'traction', but it means sketching pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sketches humorous or satirical pictures for papers is an artist who draws.

clue.text: Countryside path, rural, neat, it's redeveloped

indicators.note: redeveloped means rebuilt to a new plan, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: only IT is used; the 's stands for 'is' and joins the indicator

explanation.surface: A tidy country walk has been rebuilt by planners.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'it's redeveloped' the 's means 'is', so only IT joins RURAL and NEAT in the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A walking route through woods or fields, with signs pointing out wildlife and plants, is a countryside path.

clue.text: Writer's term for London I've lost unfortunately

indicators.note: term means end, so only the closing letter of London is taken
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author laments losing a word they had for the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term for London' looks like a nickname for the city; it is its last letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes long works of fiction is one kind of writer.

clue.text: Cricket side, that group, stop getting better

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
them refers to a group of people

explanation.surface: A cricket team seems to be asking a group to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom describes someone recovering from illness or a situation improving.

clue.text: Drink before start of race — be quick

indicators.note: start of takes only the opening letter of the word race

explanation.surface: Advice to hurry: have a cuppa before the race begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the answer rhymes with 'pear': to tear along is to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush or dash at great speed, as in tearing down the road.

clue.text: Grossly unequal? Indeed so, sadly!

indicators.note: sadly here means badly or in a poor state, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A rueful agreement that something is grossly unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest or argument where one party dominates completely is lopsided and grossly unequal.

clue.text: Extremely short, the old complaint

indicators.note: Extremely picks only the outermost letters of the word short

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the

explanation.surface: A brief old ailment, or something terse about an old complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' in the sense of a minor medical ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the eyelid is a minor medical complaint or ailment.

clue.text: Legislature against initially granting remissions easily, says spokesman

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: A spokesman claims a law-making body opposes letting prisoners off sentences lightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'says spokesman' looks like attribution, but its first letters, S and S, end the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The US federal law-making body, made up of Senate and House, is a legislature.

clue.text: Attempt to cover alien, explosive, German writer

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering means sitting above, so the attempt comes first

explanation.surface: A volatile German author tries to hide a space creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' works because this is a down entry: whatever covers sits on top, so the attempt is written above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe wrote Faust and is Germany's most celebrated author.

clue.text: Agitators half of them impatient cutting charges

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the middle pieces go inside the charges
half of takes the latter two letters of the four in them

explanation.surface: Restless troublemakers, half of them eager to slash fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of them' is the back half of the word, not a share of the agitators; 'cutting' means the pieces go inside the charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Political rabble-rousers stir up crowds by appealing to prejudice, so they are agitators.

clue.text: Instant credit

explanation.surface: Buying now, paying later: instant credit.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal usage gives both a brief moment and a deferred-payment arrangement.

clue.text: Verify pronouncement of European national

indicators.note: pronouncement means saying out loud, so the answer sounds like the word for the national

parts.note: a person from the Czech Republic is a European national

explanation.surface: An official asks to confirm what a European citizen has stated.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm the truth or accuracy of something by examining it.

clue.text: On return, mentioned holding operations typical of tyrant

indicators.note: on return means the whole assembled string is read backwards
holding means containing, so operations go inside mentioned

parts.note: cited means mentioned or referred to

explanation.surface: Returning, someone reports operations being held, the hallmark of a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: CITED holding OPS gives CITOPSED, which 'On return' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler wielding unchecked power behaves in an oppressive, autocratic way.

clue.text: Positive welcome for letter from abroad

explanation.surface: A cheery greeting in a letter sent from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter from abroad' is not post but a foreign alphabet's character.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenty-first character of the Greek alphabet is a letter from abroad.

clue.text: Beer stocked by the German trader

indicators.note: stocked by means held inside, so the beer sits within the article

explanation.surface: A German merchant stocks beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant who buys and sells goods, such as an antiques or car merchant.

clue.text: Have high regard for management about to replace unspecified number

indicators.note: replace means a new piece takes the place of an old one in the word

parts.note: admin is short for administration, management
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Respect for bosses who are poised to swap out an unknown quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect, esteem or look up to someone.

clue.text: Be fond of fellow variable at first becoming refined?

indicators.note: at first puts the fellow and variable in front

explanation.surface: Someone becomes polished by admiring a changeable man.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished, genteel, behaving with the decorum expected of a well-bred woman.
